channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Billions Allocated to Regions, But Results Unclear in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is facing issues with unspent development funds totaling 5.2 billion soms allocated to regions, and municipal enterprises remain dependent on budget subsidies instead of generating revenue. Local authorities are questioned on their effective use of allocated funds. President Sadyr Japarov raised these concerns at a recent meeting, highlighting that increased funding alone does not guarantee economic development for the regions.

item.title: New Head Appointed for Kazakhstan Temir Zholy National Railway Company
item.description: Ersayin Nagaspayev has been appointed as the new head of Kazakhstan Temir Zholy (KTZ), the national railway company. The decision was made by the board of Samruk-Kazyna. Nagaspayev previously served as the Minister of Industry and Construction. The Prime Minister emphasized priorities including transit, infrastructure, and anti-corruption.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Ministry Warns Against Using Used Oil for Heating
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Environment warns against the increasing advertising of heating stoves that use used motor oil. The ministry states that burning such fuel pollutes the air with harmful substances like soot and carbon monoxide, posing health risks. It urges citizens and businesses to refrain from this practice.

item.title: Bishkek Hosts Republican Forum on Preventing Adolescent Violence and Abuse
item.description: A republican forum titled "My Voice - My Future" was held in Bishkek to address the prevention of violence, offenses, and discrimination among adolescents. Over 400 representatives from state bodies, NGOs, educators, students, and parents participated. Discussions focused on protecting children's rights, creating safe school environments, and preventing juvenile delinquency.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Ready to Collaborate with Russia on New Energy and Digitalization Projects
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's First Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers, Daniyar Amangeldiev, met with Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak in Moscow. The officials discussed trade and economic cooperation, with a focus on energy and digitalization. Amangeldiev emphasized strengthening the strategic partnership, and Novak expressed readiness to support joint initiatives.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Become First Central Asian Nation with Four Satellite Operators
item.description: Kazakhstan is set to become the first country in Central Asia to host four satellite operators. This development signifies a significant advancement in the region's telecommunications and space technology infrastructure, enhancing connectivity and service diversity.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Introduces 'Don't Be Afraid, Report!' Feature for School Violence
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has introduced the 'Don't Be Afraid, Report!' feature within the 'E-Kündölük' application, allowing students to anonymously report incidents of violence. The Ministry of Education is working to automate the mechanism and enhance inter-agency cooperation. Over 15,000 teachers have been trained on violence prevention.

item.title: Uzbekistan Considers Harsher Penalties for Foreign Military Service and Recruitment
item.description: Uzbekistan's lower house of parliament has approved a bill to toughen criminal penalties for citizens serving in foreign militaries or law enforcement, and for those who recruit them. The proposed changes aim to address an increase in Uzbek citizens involved in foreign armed conflicts. If enacted, penalties for recruitment could range from five to ten years imprisonment.

item.title: UN Chief Warns Artificial Intelligence Poses Existential Threat to Humanity
item.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres has warned that the uncontrolled use of artificial intelligence (AI) poses growing risks. He stressed the need for international cooperation and effective safety mechanisms to manage AI's rapid development. Guterres highlighted AI's potential benefits but also its dangers, including exacerbating global inequality, citing concerns raised by AI developers themselves.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Population Deposits Grow to 30.67 Trillion Tenge
item.description: By October 1, 2026, individual deposits in Kazakh banks reached 30.67 trillion tenge, up 15.9% year-on-year. Deposits in the national currency increased by 22.8%. Long-term deposits amounted to 8.64 trillion tenge, with Otbasy Bank leading in growth and volume.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Introduce New Social Benefit Allocation System in 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to implement a new social benefit system from January 1, 2027, linking eligibility to family welfare levels determined by a digital family map. This aims to reallocate social spending based on income, assets, and employment.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Outlines Key Tasks for New National Railways Chief
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov introduced Yerzhan Nagaspayev as the new chairman of Kazakhstan Temir Zholy (KTZ). Bektenov emphasized expanding transport and logistics potential, increasing transit cargo, developing infrastructure, and improving company efficiency. Strengthening corporate discipline and anti-corruption efforts were also highlighted.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Russia to Strengthen Energy and Digital Cooperation
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's First Deputy Prime Minister Daniyar Amangeldiev met with Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak in Moscow. They discussed current issues in Kyrgyz-Russian trade and economic cooperation, particularly in the energy and digitalization sectors. Both sides expressed readiness to expand mutually beneficial cooperation and advance joint initiatives.

item.title: Human Rights Group Reports Denial of HIV Treatment in Turkmenistan
item.description: The Turkmen Helsinki Foundation for Human Rights expressed concern over reports of medication denial for HIV patients in Turkmenistan, discrimination, and the government's concealment of the epidemic's scale. The foundation stated this practice violates citizens' constitutional right to healthcare. Reports indicate worsening conditions and fatalities due to lack of treatment.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Over 90% of phones verified without issues, says Ministry of Digital Development
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Digital Development reports that over 90% of mobile devices are successfully verified under new registration rules. Since March 25, 2025, a centralized system tracks devices by IMEI, with a 30-day verification period. Unverified devices face a network block. Approximately 9% of devices, often imported, encounter verification problems.

item.title: CPJ urges US to release detained Afghan journalist facing deportation
item.description: The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) is calling for the immediate release of Afghan journalist Shaban Ali Rafat, detained in the US since January 2025. CPJ warns that deporting him to Afghanistan risks persecution due to his work and Hazara ethnicity. A magistrate judge recommended his release, but he remains detained pending a December 8 hearing.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Harsher Penalties for Foreign Military Service and Recruitment
item.description: Uzbekistan's Legislative Chamber approved a bill to increase criminal liability for citizens serving in foreign militaries or law enforcement agencies, and for those involved in recruiting them. The proposed changes aim to address the rising number of Uzbek citizens being drawn into foreign armed conflicts, with a reported 12-fold increase in such offenses.

item.title: US Official Discusses Energy and Transport Cooperation in Ashgabat
item.description: A US official held talks in Ashgabat focusing on enhancing trade, investment, energy cooperation, and developing Trans-Caspian transport routes. The US reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening relations with Turkmenistan and conveyed greetings from President Trump. Both sides expressed optimism about boosting bilateral ties and discussed cooperation with American companies.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Orders Wider 5G Network Application
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov has instructed the Ministry of Digital Development to ensure broader application of 5G networks in industry and transport. The goal is to achieve tangible economic benefits beyond just faster mobile internet. The ministry must identify priority sectors and enterprises for private 5G network implementation by the end of Q1 2027.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Legalizes Digital Evidence and Seizure of Virtual Assets
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has legalized digital evidence and the seizure of virtual assets in criminal cases through a new law signed by President Sadyr Japarov. The law introduces criminal liability for securities market manipulation and establishes rules for handling digital evidence. Most provisions take effect six months after official publication.

item.title: Kazakhstan Minister Addresses SKAI AI's Role Amid "Samruk-Kazyna" Corruption Scandal
item.description: Kazakhstan's Minister of Digital Development, Innovation and Aerospace Industry, Zhaslan Madiev, clarified the role of the SKAI AI system within the "Samruk-Kazyna" fund amidst a corruption scandal. He stated SKAI operates as an independent director and its decisions are within the board's competence. The AI, implemented in October 2025, is being examined following the detention of "Samruk-Kazyna" and "Kazakhstan Temir Zholy" chairmen.

item.title: Kyrgyz agricultural institutions receive 179 million som equipment donation
item.description: Seventy units of agricultural machinery worth 179 million som were transferred to two agrarian research institutions in Kyrgyzstan. The equipment, acquired through a World Bank project, includes tractors, combines, and specialized machinery to improve seed systems and provide quality seeds and seedlings to farmers.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Armenia aim to expand trade and economic cooperation
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and Armenia intend to expand their trade and economic cooperation, as discussed during a meeting between the Deputy Foreign Minister of Kyrgyzstan and the Armenian Ambassador. They reviewed the implementation of agreements from President Sapar Japarov's visit to Yerevan and discussed a roadmap for cooperation until 2029.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Tashkent Region Police Conclude 20-Day Security Operation
item.description: A 20-day operation in Uzbekistan's Tashkent Region resulted in 233 criminal cases, the resolution of 369 previously unsolved crimes, and the apprehension of 117 wanted individuals. Authorities seized nearly 30 kilograms of narcotics and 16 units of homemade and pneumatic weapons. Cybercrime investigations also led to the resolution of 262 digital technology-related offenses.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: MPs Receive Closed-Door Briefing on 'Kundoluk' Electronic System
item.description: Members of Kyrgyzstan's Jogorku Kenesh are receiving a closed-door briefing on the automated information system 'Kundoluk' in schools. The Ministry of Education requested the secrecy. This follows a scandal where developers accused the ministry of pressuring schools to switch to a new version of the system, which the ministry claims is a free state service.

item.title: Kazakhstan Aims to Compete with SpaceX in the Global Space Market
item.description: Kazakhstan aims to challenge Elon Musk's SpaceX in the global space market, leveraging its Baikonur Cosmodrome and integrated space industry. The country seeks to develop its own launch capabilities and secure a niche in the satellite launch sector. Additionally, Kazakhstan plans to move beyond raw material extraction in critical minerals, focusing on processing and battery production.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan launches anti-fraud system for cybercrime in test mode
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has launched an anti-fraud system to combat cybercrime in test mode. The system will connect 26 commercial banks, allowing authorities to freeze funds for up to 30 days to prevent illegal money withdrawal. This initiative follows successful implementation in Uzbekistan.

item.title: Kazakhstan investigates alleged data leak from Supreme Court
item.description: Kazakhstan is investigating reports of a potential data leak from the Supreme Court, according to Deputy Prime Minister Zhanat Madiev. The Committee for Information Security and the National Security Committee are conducting the probe. Madiev noted that claims of personal data appearing in the darknet are frequent but often contain irrelevant information.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Digital Development Ministry Tasked with Enhancing Cybersecurity Measures
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov has instructed the Ministry of Digital Development to improve the effectiveness of cybersecurity efforts. The ministry must identify vulnerabilities, secure key communication channels, and regularly test operator readiness for emergencies within three months. The goal is to prevent cyberattacks and ensure the resilience of critical communication networks.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Digital Ministry to Disclose Results of Probe into Yandex Service Outage
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Digital Development will publicly share findings from the prosecutor's investigation into the Yandex service outage. Deputy Prime Minister Zhaslan Madiev stated that while such checks can be routine, any publicly releasable information regarding data protection and cross-border data transfer will be disclosed. The outage on October 11 was linked to an attack on a Russian data center.

item.title: South Korea Scrambles Jets as Russian Military Aircraft Enter Air Defense Zone
item.description: South Korean military scrambled fighter jets and issued an air alert on November 24 after several Russian military aircraft entered the country's air defense identification zone over the Sea of Japan. The aircraft did not violate South Korean airspace. Seoul plans to protest the incident.

item.title: Uzbekistan Convenes Intellectuals Council for New Phase of State-Society Dialogue
item.description: The first meeting of the Council of Intellectuals of Uzbekistan was held in Tashkent, aiming to unite the nation's intellectual potential and expand the participation of intellectuals in societal development. Saida Mirziyoyeva emphasized the council's role in fostering open dialogue and receiving candid feedback for state policy.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Secures $30 Million in Climate Finance at COP31
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has secured $30 million in climate finance, with a focus on protecting mountainous regions from climate change impacts. The country chaired a group of 12 mountainous nations at the summit. Discussions also covered fossil fuel phase-out, energy security, and developed nations' climate responsibilities.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Considers Stricter Rules for Migrant Parents' Child Custody
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Labor is proposing legal agreements for migrant citizens to formalize child custody with relatives. This aims to increase accountability for parents working abroad, addressing concerns about child neglect and legal violations. The ministry reported 84,000 children left behind by migrant parents.

item.title: Three Microfinance Organizations in Kazakhstan Lose Licenses for Violations
item.description: Kazakhstan's Agency for Regulation and Development of the Financial Market has revoked the licenses of three microfinance organizations: 'ECKZ' LLP, 'Taj Finance' LLP, and 'M Bulak' LLP. The decision, made on November 23, cites systematic violations of legal requirements and harm to consumer rights.

item.title: Tashkent Land Plot Near Metro Station Sold for 244.27 Billion Soums
item.description: A land plot in Tashkent's Yashnabad district was sold at auction for 244.27 billion soums. The Comfortdrive company made the sole bid, exceeding the starting price by 1%. The 2.59-hectare plot is located near the Mashinasozlar metro station.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Police Officer Among Suspects in Talas Assault Case
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Interior Ministry announced a criminal case in Talas, where a group assaulted an individual, has been reclassified under attempted murder. Initially, charges were filed under hooliganism. One of the nine detained suspects is a police officer. The ministry detailed two separate incidents on November 17 and 20, involving beatings and a vehicle assault.

item.title: UN: Over 47,000 Women and Girls Killed by Intimate Partners or Family in 2025
item.description: A new UN report indicates that over 47,000 women and girls worldwide were killed by their husbands, partners, or family members in 2025, averaging five victims per hour. The report highlights the persistent nature of domestic violence, with approximately 60% of intentional homicides against women committed by someone close. This data emerges amid concerns for women's rights in Afghanistan.

item.title: Iran Pursues Dual Strategy Amidst Persian Gulf Tensions and US Naval Blockade
item.description: Iran faces a "neither war nor peace" situation in the Persian Gulf due to a US naval blockade, impacting its oil exports and economy. Officials view this as an existential threat, driving Tehran to seek a resolution through diplomatic channels, including using Qatar to relay messages to the US government.

item.title: Former Industry Minister Appointed Head of Kazakhstan Railways Amid Corruption Probe
item.description: Former Industry and Construction Minister Yersaiyn Nagaspayev has been appointed chairman of Kazakhstan's national railway company, Kazakhstan Temir Zholy (KTZ). This follows the arrest of the previous head, Yeldas Otinsheyev, and the chairman of the Samruk-Kazyna sovereign wealth fund on corruption charges.
